items.basis: The proposed mechanism fails to address the fundamental physics of peristaltic pumps where occlusion forces are inherently concentrated by the rotor design, and attempting to "dynamically redistribute pressure" would require fundamentally changing the pump's operating principle which contradicts the basic peristaltic function described in evidence [doi:10.1016/s0262-1762(03)00715-6]

The candidate completely ignores critical boundary conditions including fluid viscosity variations, temperature fluctuations, and tubing material properties that significantly affect occlusion force distribution as documented in evidence [doi:10.1186/s13244-024-01750-4], making the proposed solution unreliable across real-world operating conditions

The candidate's prediction of extending tubing service life beyond 500 hours directly contradicts evidence [doi:10.32786/2071-9485-2018-03-324-329] which demonstrates that peristaltic pump tubing failure is primarily a material fatigue issue that cannot be solved by force redistribution alone

The candidate provides no evidence that their solution maintains 0.5 mL/min flow with better than 2% dosing accuracy under the same conditions as the baseline, which is a critical requirement for a dosing pump in a water quality analyzer where precision is paramount

Integrating a miniaturized pressure transducer and flow monitoring system within the pump head would require significant redesign of the compact pump head, likely increasing its size and complexity beyond the compact form factor required for benchtop water-quality analyzers as evidenced by [doi:10.1016/s0262-1762(04)00163-4]

The testable prediction fails to specify critical measurement parameters including the definition of "localized fatigue," acceptable pressure variation thresholds, and failure criteria, making the accelerated life testing impossible to properly validate as described in evidence [doi:10.52338/jows.2026.5561]
